hook.line: How to get an AI co-founder that works on your startup 24/7 on autopilot.
hook.visual: Masked presenter in cap points at camera; top half builds an 'AI runs your company' node diagram; white title pill 'AI Builds Your Company On Autopilot' with emojis.

beats.what: Split screen: animated node diagram on top, masked presenter below, title pill across the seam, word captions on his chest
Cut to full-screen 'topmast' logo over a dark app UI card: the product he built
Cut to Polsia screen recording, 'Let's build something' page, with zoom punches as he clicks
'What's your idea?' form with the startup typed in, then continue
Task list view: 'Polsia completed six tasks' over the list of finished jobs
Animated 'Polsia' title with an hour 1-8 timeline; task cards slide in one by one (product updates, tested app)
More cards slide past in sync with the voice: dashboards, SEO FAQ page, marketing content, email outreach
Back to screen recording: 'Auto Mode' dialog, it keeps finding new tasks
Hand holds a phone showing his TikTok profile: link in bio
Presenter points down to a 'POLSIA' comment-keyword pill

why_it_works: Promise and visual answer in the first second: the 'AI runs your company' diagram builds while he says the claim, so the eye has something to decode before the first cut
The proof is a timeline: hour markers plus task cards sliding in one per spoken task turn 'six tasks in eight hours' into something you watch happen
Comment-a-keyword CTA ('POLSIA') with a pill graphic and a pointing gesture converts viewers into comments, which feeds reach
Steps are shown in the real product UI with zoom punches on each click, so it reads as a tutorial you could follow
weaknesses: Face is masked, so there is no expression; trust rests entirely on the screen proof
68% of text sits outside the safe area, and the small 'fake UI' text in the timeline cards is hard to read at phone size
Middle section is a stream of feature nouns read at 3.3 words/s with no pause or payoff moment
for_robert: Copy the 'proof timeline': when he lists what a tool did, have each item slide in as a card on cue, with Fred tapping each card as it lands so the list becomes a sequence of small events.
